registered_boundary_sensitivity.definition: one extra edge after fill-to-service and after a previously occupied buffer is released; sensitivity only, not implemented RTL

hammer_findings.finding: The sealed checksum manifest is internally valid, pins the analyzer, contract, result, README, prior M195 review and unchanged docs/359, and all 120 frozen FC2 payloads pass independent SHA, extent and popcount checks.

An independently authored decoder and finite-buffer recurrence reproduce all aggregate and per-stage M196 values exactly. Pair/tail conservation closes, zero tokens remain token-local, and no cross-token pair is constructed.

The decision to reject F1 buffer-only promotion is justified at the declared D={2,4,8,8} point. B2 is 0.3081% slower, B3 is 0.0208% slower, and the uncharged B4 storage/control point gains only 0.2237%.

The same decision survives a stricter registered boundary attack: B2 and B3 remain slower and B4 gains only 0.2155%. This increases confidence in the negative decision but does not establish the absolute cycle count of future RTL.

Within the sealed one-descriptor-per-cycle recurrence, descriptor arrival and pair readiness are the exposed bottleneck: replay-only pair work is 71,596,122 cycles, yet B2 wall time is 97,909,442. This supports investigating packed ingress, not claiming that packed ingress is already beneficial.

The producer is an idealized preindexed nonzero-descriptor stream. A two-descriptor fill point is inadmissible unless the scanner/compactor can actually discover, tag and accept two nonzeros per cycle without an oracle, including tails, bubbles and backpressure.

No executable queue/head/SRAM-response/Acc24 path fixes the fill-close, issue-start, response-return, buffer-release and token-done edges. Absolute finite cycles remain exact only under the abstract recurrence; arbitrary response/result stalls and stale responses across reset/token rearm are open.

The rejection is specific to F=1 and D={2,4,8,8}; it is not a global proof against every buffer/depth/ingress co-design. Any packed-ingress follow-on must report the matched baseline, buffer bits, write ports, compactor/control area, timing and energy.

B3/B4 only change stage 3 at this maximum-window geometry; stages 0-2 have no more than two windows per token. The aggregate improvement therefore cannot be presented as a generally effective multi-buffer mechanism.

p0_before_packed_ingress_speedup_admissi: Build an exact-payload packed-ingress DSE that charges the real number of descriptors accepted per cycle and preserves descriptor index, bank population, token/window identity and odd-tail ordering without a nonzero oracle.

Implement the selected packer plus finite token-owned queues/head advancement and exercise VCS with all 120 payloads, zero tokens, odd tails, full buffers and arbitrary descriptor/issue/response/result stalls.

Carry epoch plus token/window/request identity through SRAM request/response and prove stale responses cannot update a rearmed token; release a pair only after all logical queues and outstanding responses retire.
Run matched Synopsys DC/STA and charge packed write paths, buffer storage/control and any wider producer interface before admitting a throughput/area advantage.
p1_for_complete_fc2: Pin one edge-accurate handshake recurrence to the RTL and rerun exact payload cycles with measured SRAM latency and output backpressure.
Include BN2, residual/ATLIF commit, final-token drain and token header/done work.
Report macro area/access energy and compare any alternative buffer/depth point under equal storage and port assumptions.
Add an exact invocation/runner receipt to the sealed DSE package for path-independent reproduction.
